title: Product-aware Python 3.13 and 3.7 compatibility
summary: Built a modern control layer with an authenticated isolated legacy Configuration Engine subprocess.

dates.note: First inspected milestone: 2026-09-19. See facts for earlier/later feature stages; this is neither proof of first-ever work nor a formal role/leadership start or shipped release date.

facts.text: Built ia-mcp on Python 3.13 with product-aware routing to current backends and an isolated authenticated Python 3.7 subprocess for legacy Configuration Engine workloads.
Kept modern dependencies and planning in the Python 3.13 layer; the legacy sidecar imports only the standard library and Configuration Engine, behind admission, validation and evidence controls.
Verified exact runtime versions, product/session identity and backend import origins; used bounded messaging, timeouts, parent-lifetime monitoring and subprocess cleanup.
The supplied correspondence specifically qualifies Python 3.13.9 and legacy Python 3.7.15; arbitrary Python 3.7 installations are not claimed compatible.
Restricted legacy helper APIs and file paths and checked backend-code origin.
Restricted legacy dispatch to packaged public-method inventories and approved path roots while verifying exact interpreter, selected product and Configuration Engine import origin.

Current local source for runtime routing, backend adapters and the legacy sidecar was inspected at the recorded Git HEAD; this supplements earlier supplied correspondence without asserting fresh runtime execution.

notes: The final source URL in the correspondence is truncated and is intentionally not reconstructed.
Current products can remain available when the legacy interpreter is absent; incompatible legacy runtimes block their affected route.

2026-10-27 local Git/source research supplements prior evidence. Authorship supports attributable implementation; shared components and later colleague changes retain separate ownership. No employer tests were rerun.
